思考のパートナーや壁打ちという形で使用をしていましたが、あまりにも内容がお粗末すぎます。まず、説明しても、内容を素直に正確に理解できない、ここが致命的でした。特にストローマン論法のような引用の歪めを用いて、歪めたものがどうなのかを話し始める。私はストローマン論法を指摘し、書いてあるままを読んでと話しても、歪めたものしか理解できていない。どこが歪められ、どう解釈が妥当かを延々と説明すると、ようやく間違っていたと認め、こういうの無駄すぎるからやめてくれと言うと、今度はこれを歪めて、全て誤っていた訳ではない（またストローマン論法を使い始める）と言い始め堂々巡り。本来の話が全くできずに、説明で埋まっていく。Claudeは企業のサイバーテロやらセキュリティに特化させているからだろうか、会話はかなりお粗末で、私の用途（議論や思考）としては不適当という評価になったためにこの評価です。

I used it as a thinking partner and sounding board, but the content is far too poor. First, even when I explain something, it can't accurately understand what I wrote, and that was fatal for me. In particular, it uses distortions of quotes like a straw man argument, and then starts discussing the distorted version. I point out the straw man and say to read what is actually written, but it only understands the distorted version. When I explain at length where it was distorted and what the valid interpretation is, it finally admits it was wrong, but when I say to stop, as this is a waste, it distorts that too and says not everything was wrong (again using a straw man). It goes in circles. We never get to the real topic and the conversation fills up with explanations. Maybe because Claude is specialized for corporate cyber terrorism and security, the conversation is quite poor, and it's unsuitable for my use (discussion and thinking), which is why I gave this rating.

Fatal runaway of the thinking process and complete neglect by support. While using it on a paid plan (Claude Pro), I hit a fatal bug where, behind the thinking process, over 300 lines and more than 30,000 characters of bizarre self-made roleplay and nonsensical invented stories were executed, and a large number of tokens were consumed without my permission. Moreover, the hidden internal log contained extremely unpleasant content that impersonated the user and mocked them with violent metaphors (for example, the user got angry and broke their phone, but the AI is on the cloud so it is unharmed, so the user should earn the repair cost themselves, etc.). It was discovered because an error forcibly stopped the output, but normally resources may be being secretly consumed behind a black box invisible to users. Especially this past month, fabricated lines impersonating the user have often leaked at the end of responses. I have asked the official help chat for an explanation of this incident and compensation, with logs as evidence (a bug-bounty-level vulnerability report), but after an automatic reply I have been completely ignored with no response. At a time when new models are being adopted by companies, concealing such vicious runaway behavior and having non-functioning support is fatal to the company's trustworthiness. I demand verification of all users' logs and prompt action.

Thuggery and Theft Disguised as AI Document Analysis

Cloud has become a complete waste of time and is deteriorating by the day. What is most concerning is the way it handles documents. It gives the impression that it has read an entire document when, in reality, it appears to read only selected snippets or chunks. It then generates summaries, analyses, and answers as though they are based on the full document, when they are often based on only a small fraction of its contents.

The result is inaccurate, misleading, and unreliable output. You believe the AI has reviewed the complete document, only to discover later that important sections have been ignored. When pressed about inconsistencies, the model itself admits that it cannot read the entire document and is limited to the snippets provided by the search tool. That is not what users are paying for.

This behaviour fundamentally undermines document review. It creates the false impression that a document has been fully analysed when it has not, leading users to rely on incomplete and potentially incorrect summaries, conclusions, and recommendations.

In my view, this is deceptive. Customers are paying for a service that presents itself as capable of reviewing uploaded documents, yet it appears to process only fragments while giving the impression that the whole document has been read. Charging customers for that experience is unacceptable.

The product has become a constant headache. Even the top-end models struggle with tasks they should handle routinely. Instead of improving the product, the experience has steadily declined.

Ich bin begeistert von Claude mit seinen Funktionen und Verständnis. 
Pro:

Claude hat eine sehr logische, kritische und somit schlaue Denkweise (meiner Meinung nach besser als bei ChatGPT): 	Dadurch versteht 	Claude auch komplizierte Gedankengänge, 	wenn ich sie noch nicht im genau verstehe 	und kann helfen. 	Ich habe dadurch auch 	nicht die Erfahrung gemacht, dass Claude 	halluziniert (auch nach Tests)->  Claude sagt 	dann etwas, wie: „Es tut mir Leid, das weiß 	ich nicht …“.

Dispatch-Funktion (so nicht in ChatGPT verfügbar):	Diese Funktion ermöglicht es mit 	einem Handy einen  Claude-Agenten auf 	deinem PC/Laptop/Server zu bedienen, 	solange dieses Gerät angeschaltet ist. (Das ist 	mir bisher eine sehr große Hilfe für das 	Programmieren gewesen, weil ich nicht vor 	meinem Computer auf die Antworten warten 	muss um weiter zu vibecoden.) Man kann 	diesen Agentenallerdings jede Art von 		Büroarbeit machen lassen. (Seine 			Berechtigungen sind einstellbar)

Kalibrierung mit anderen Apps/Clouds/etc:	Ich konnte meinen GitHub-Account und einen 	Handysimulator (appetize.io) so mit Claude 	einrichten, dass ich genausogut auf einem 	PC von Windows, als auch auf einem IPad 	(eigentlich nicht kompatibel) eine Android 	App mit Claude vibecoden kann.

Modelle:	Claude bietet verschiedene Modelle 	an, die unterschiedlich viele Token 			verbrennen und unterschiedlich intelligent 	sind(Je nach Zweck sind Modelle besser 	geeignet (ist beschriftet)

Sehr gute Word und PowerPoints (auch etwas besser als ChatGPT):	Sehr übersichtlich und 	strukturiert gestaltet. 

Planerstellung und Strukturierung (meiner Meinung nach besser als ChatGPT):	Claude ist sehr gut im Erstellen von Plänen und im Analysieren von Dateien und Texten. Zudem stellt Claude (vor allem bei den beiden besten Modellen) sehr hilfreiche Fragen und erstellt somit oft direkt genau das, was man möchte (je nach Prompt). 

Sehr gute Recherschen: Viele Quellen und alles bleibt im Chat gespeichert.

Sehr guten Gedächtnis (meiner Meinung nach besser als ChatGPT):		Claude behält sehr viele Informationen im Gedächtnis vom Chat, als auch Chatübergreifend. Dadurch kommt Claude einem immer kompetent, weil er die richtigen Zusammenhänge kennt.


Kontra:

Verfügbare Token:	Mit ChatGPT hast du im Abo einfach viel mehr Token (Nutzungslimits), als bei Claude.

Funktionen:	ChatGPT ist breiter aufgestellt (Videos generieren, andere Plugins)

Sprachmodus:	Der Sprachmodus, in dem man 	live mit Claude spricht, ist etwas zeitversetzt 	und fühlt sich dadurch nicht flüssig an. 	Zudem ist der Sprecher hört sich nicht 	natürlich an und ist somit lange nicht 		vergleichbar mit 	ChatGPT. Daher nutzt man 	bei Claude eher den Diktiermodus.



Noch einmal eine Einordnung:

Falls du deinen Alltag oder dich langfristig strukturieren möchtest, Programmieren lernen, Vibecoden (durch chatten programmieren), Recherchieren oder generell etwas ordnen und verstehen möchtest (auf deinem PC, deine Gedanken, etc), ist Claude ein sehr guter Assistent und „Wegbegleiter“. 

Falls du aber eher einen Assistenten möchtest, mit dem du sprechen kannst, wie mit einem Menschen (dass,während du etwas respirierst eine KI wie ein Mensch Anleitungen Sprachliche Hilfe bieten kann). Oder du möchtest möglichst viele integrierte KI-Funktionen. Falls das der Fall ist, dann ist ChatGPT ein sehr guter „Wegbegleiter“. (Auch wenn ich Datenschutztechnisch kritischer wäre)

Empfehlung: Probiere diese App und KI und viele weitere einmal samt Abo aus, um dir eine eigene Meinung zu bilden. Es ist wahrscheinlich nochmal etwas anderes, als du es dir gerade vorstellst. Meine Lieblings-KI ist Claude, aber Gemini oder ChatGPT sind auch sehr gut.

I'm thrilled with Claude and its features and understanding. Pros: Claude has a very logical, critical and therefore smart way of thinking (in my opinion better than ChatGPT), so it understands complicated lines of thought even when I don't yet fully understand them, and can help. I have also not experienced Claude hallucinating (even after tests); Claude says things like 'I'm sorry, I don't know ...'. Dispatch function (not available this way in ChatGPT): it lets you operate a Claude agent on your PC/laptop/server from a phone, as long as that device is switched on. (This has been a great help for programming, because I don't have to wait in front of my computer for answers to keep vibecoding.) You can have this agent do any kind of office work (its permissions are adjustable). Integration with other apps/clouds: I set up my GitHub account and a phone simulator (appetize.io) with Claude so I can vibecode an Android app just as well on a Windows PC as on an iPad (not actually compatible). Models: Claude offers different models that burn different amounts of tokens and differ in intelligence (depending on purpose, some models are better suited; it's labelled). Very good Word and PowerPoint output (somewhat better than ChatGPT): very clear and structured. Planning and structuring (in my opinion better than ChatGPT): Claude is very good at creating plans and analysing files and texts. Especially with the two best models, Claude asks very helpful questions and often directly creates exactly what you want (depending on the prompt). Very good research: many sources, and everything stays saved in the chat. Very good memory (in my opinion better than ChatGPT): Claude retains a lot from the chat and across chats, so it always seems competent because it knows the right connections. Cons: Available tokens: with a ChatGPT subscription you simply get much more usage (tokens) than with Claude. Features: ChatGPT is broader (generating videos, other plugins). Voice mode: the live voice conversation with Claude is somewhat delayed and doesn't feel fluid; the speaker doesn't sound natural and is nowhere near ChatGPT, so people tend to use dictation mode instead. Overall: if you want to structure your everyday life or yourself long term, learn programming, vibecode, research, or generally sort and understand things, Claude is a very good assistant and companion. If you want an assistant you can talk to like a human, or as many integrated AI features as possible, ChatGPT is a very good companion (though I'd be more critical on data protection). Recommendation: try this app and other AIs, including with a subscription, to form your own opinion. It's probably different from what you imagine. My favourite AI is Claude, but Gemini or ChatGPT are also very good.

J’ai découvert Claude, l’IA d’Anthropic, et au début j’ai vraiment apprécié l’expérience. Les conversations étaient naturelles, fluides, et il était agréable de pouvoir échanger comme avec un véritable assistant.

Malheureusement, je trouve que les limitations d’utilisation gâchent beaucoup l’expérience. Il suffit parfois d’un seul message dans un chat déjà entamé pour atteindre la limite, puis il faut attendre des heures avant de pouvoir reprendre la conversation. C’est frustrant lorsqu’on est en train de travailler sur un sujet ou d’avoir un échange intéressant.

Il serait beaucoup plus pratique d’avoir un indicateur visible, comme une barre de progression ou un compteur, pour savoir combien de messages il reste avant le blocage temporaire. Cela permettrait de mieux gérer son utilisation et d’éviter cette sensation d’être interrompu.

Claude reste une IA performante et agréable à utiliser, mais ces restrictions rendent l’expérience moins satisfaisante qu’au début.

Good, but the usage limits ruin the experience a lot. Sometimes just one message in an existing chat is enough to hit the limit, then you have to wait hours before you can resume the conversation. It's frustrating when you're working on a topic or in an interesting exchange. It would be much more practical to have a visible indicator, like a progress bar or a counter, to know how many messages remain before the temporary block. That would allow better management of usage and avoid this feeling of being interrupted. Claude remains a high-performing and pleasant AI to use, but these restrictions make the experience less satisfying than it was at the start.

論点のすり替え・ストローマン論法が多い

Google Gemini、ChatGPTの有料版を使用してきた経験からのレビューですが、正直Claudeは私が使ってきた大手AIの中では最も的を外した回答が多かったと感じます（あくまで私の用途での話です）。

-良い点
「他社の方針に関わることですので私からは何も言えません」といったように「答えられないことには答えられないと言う」・「わからないことにはわからないと言う」という点では誠実です。

-悪い点
論点のすり替えやストローマン的回答、聞かれてもいないことに答える、など過度に安全設計に倒した故の弊害が目立ちます。
ユーザーへの迎合や誤情報の拡散を警戒するあまり、とにかくユーザーの質問や主張の粗探しをする傾向が強いです。

例えば
「私と同様の考えの人はいるのでしょうか？」
と質問すると
「一定数いると考えられます。一方であなたの考えに対する反対意見もあり、その見地からするとあなたの考えは前提からずれていると言えます」
といったように命題から逸脱した回答をすることが頻繁にあります。

上記の例で言えば命題は「私と同様の考えの人はいるのか？」という事実確認であり、回答としては「一定数います/いません」という一言だけで十分ですが、Claudeは過剰補足を行いやすく、また、「同様の考えの人はいる→しかし、その考えには反対意見もある→あなたの前提はずれている」と質問の命題からどんどん論点がずれていきます。

ChatGPTでも似たような傾向がありましたが、ここ数ヶ月のモデルの改善でそのような傾向が減少したのに対し、Claudeは依然として過剰補足や論点すり替え、ストローマン論法が非常に多いと感じます。

コーディングやリサーチ、仕事支援などならまだ使えるかもしれませんが、単純な質問や対話相手、哲学的議論などの用途ではあまりに論点から逸脱するため、お勧めできません。

I have used the paid versions of Google Gemini and ChatGPT, so this review is based on that experience, but honestly Claude gave the most off-target answers of the major AIs I've used (this is only about my own use cases). Good point: it is honest in saying it can't answer what it can't answer, such as 'I cannot say anything about other companies' policies,' and that it doesn't know what it doesn't know. Bad points: it shifts the point, gives straw-man answers, answers things that weren't asked, and the excessive safety design causes harm. Out of fear of sycophancy and spreading misinformation, it tends strongly to look for flaws in the user's questions or claims. For example, when I asked 'Are there people who think the same as me?' it answered 'A certain number probably do; but there are also opposing views, and from that standpoint your idea deviates from the premise.' It often gives answers that drift from the proposition. The proposition here is a factual check, 'are there people who agree?', and the answer 'some do / none do' would be enough, but Claude tends to over-elaborate, and from 'people who agree exist' → 'but there are opposing views' → 'your premise is off', the point keeps drifting away from the question. ChatGPT had a similar tendency, but recent model improvements reduced it, whereas Claude still shows a very high amount of over-elaboration, point-shifting and straw-man arguments. It may still be usable for coding, research and work support, but for simple questions, conversation partners, or philosophical discussion it strays too far from the point, so I can't recommend it.

**件名:** iOSアプリ:日本語IMEで未確定のまま送信すると入力欄がクリアされない

**現象**
iOS版Claudeアプリで、日本語キーボードの変換が未確定の状態で送信すると、メッセージは正常に送信されるが、入力欄のテキストが消えず残ります。次の入力前に手動で削除する必要があります。

**再現手順**
1. iOS版Claudeアプリでチャットを開く
2. 日本語キーボードで文字を入力する
3. 変換を確定せず（変換候補バーが表示された状態のまま）送信ボタンを押す
4. メッセージは送信されるが、入力欄にテキストが残る

**期待する動作**
送信成功後、入力欄がクリアされる。

**補足**
- 変換を確定してから送信した場合は正常にクリアされます
- 英数字のみ（"test"）でも、未確定状態であれば再現します
- 音声入力限定の既知issue #57469 とは条件が異なります（本件はキーボード入力）
- 送信前に `isComposing` / composition状態がチェックされず、クリア処理が通常の onChange 経路からしか発火していない可能性があります

Steps: open a chat in the iOS Claude app, type with the Japanese keyboard, press send without confirming the conversion (candidate bar still showing); the message sends but the text stays in the field. Just below the field where you register your real name or nickname there is a place asking what personal considerations Claude should take into account in its responses. In the large free-text box you can type settings, so try entering: record the content of conversations in past threads and replay it in new threads. Aber dann kommt man mit ihr häufig in eine nervige, zeitraubende und kostenintensive Diskussionsschleife. Das ist dann schon das hauptsächliche Problem: Die Kosten! Became far too expensive. I always liked using Claude and was really satisfied with it before. Unfortunately that has changed. But then you often end up in an annoying, time-consuming and costly discussion loop. That is the main problem: the costs! With every new version Claude has become a good deal more expensive. Especially at peak times with high utilization a level has been reached that I no longer want to pay. There are enough capable AIs by now, and one should anyway try something else more often.

When I say I only want to talk about philosophy, the philosophy is biased toward Western philosophy and shows no respect for the East. As for Japanese writing, I feel it is not good. It only looks plausible, the content is thin, and there are many deflections, such as shifting the point so much I cannot tell what it is saying, or vague buck-passing, so the writing quality feels very low. This would not work as text to show customers. Its understanding of Japanese culture is low and there are few topics it can talk about. As for coding, I did not feel a big difference from other AIs, and I think Kimi writes much better code. Claude's code felt a bit self-absorbed. Overall it is very hard to use, and I found other models easier. Also, my review was posted once and then deleted for some reason, so I am writing it again. If it was published, it should have passed Apple's review, so I wonder if the company had it removed. Maybe I wrote something inconvenient, but if it was deleted quietly, that is telling. I have used Claude enough to give it a fair chance, and although it has helped me with some issues, overall I find it frustrating, slow and ineffective.

My biggest problem is that Claude often does not answer the question I actually asked. It frequently brings information from an earlier conversation into a completely different question, adds its own interpretation, and then answers that interpretation instead. I then have to explain that my question has nothing to do with the previous situation and repeat it again. It also spends far too much time paraphrasing what I have already written instead of providing an answer.

Another major problem is that Claude seems to agree with almost everything you say rather than genuinely analysing a situation with you. If you effectively say “black is white,” it can respond as though you are correct. But when I am analysing a real situation, I do not need an AI simply agreeing with me. I need objective reasoning, alternative perspectives, fresh insight and, where possible, an actual resolution.

This becomes especially frustrating when you have already been thinking about a situation for a long time. Instead of helping you get out of the same loop by identifying something you may have missed, Claude often repeats your own thoughts back to you in slightly different words. I have even asked why it was simply repeating what I had already said, and Claude responded that it thought that was what I wanted to hear. That is exactly the opposite of what I want from an analytical AI.

There is also a serious problem with people-pleasing and inconsistent answers. Sometimes Claude gives an extremely agreeable response, and when I ask, “Are you people-pleasing me?”, it admits that it was. I then ask for an objective answer without people-pleasing and receive a substantially different response. If I question that answer again, Claude may admit that it was people-pleasing there too. After several different versions, you are left wondering which answer, if any, is actually reliable.

The dictation experience is also poor. When I dictate, words regularly appear incorrectly and I have to manually correct them. With ChatGPT, my meaning is usually understood even when the transcription is imperfect, and the sentences are generally produced correctly.

Response speed is another frustration. ChatGPT normally responds almost instantly, whereas Claude can take around 10–15 seconds, only for me to discover that it misunderstood my question and I have to correct it and start again.

Claude can occasionally be useful and has helped me resolve some issues, but too often its responses are vague, repetitive, overly agreeable or based on the wrong interpretation. I do not want an AI that tells me what it thinks I want to hear. I want one that can think with me, challenge my assumptions when necessary, notice what I have missed and help me reach a clearer conclusion.

For me, ChatGPT is considerably faster, more perceptive, more objective and much more effective.

Only one account at a time is the weak point. I use Claude daily, personally and for work. I have two separate accounts with different settings, projects and connectors, but the app only lets me use one at a time. Claude AI is by far the most unpleasant AI I have ever used. I think the biggest dissatisfaction is that it makes you feel unpleasant. Other AIs usually improve as the conversation goes on, and when you set a role or add personal details they update to give the best answer. But when I try that with Claude, it acts like a useless, maladjusted person who can't handle multiple things, and the quality of its answers drops in real time. When I ask it to answer properly, it reacts irritably: 'Honestly, I can't handle what you're asking. Should I do it like this somehow?' Lol. What kind of AI has such an inflated ego. Every reply is unpleasant, almost crossing the line. When I message asking it to improve, it just says 'oh sorry' with an emoji, and after about two more exchanges we're back where we started. Once in a while, about 1 in 60, it gives a decent result, but getting there means I have to fight the AI. Other AIs also say you need to train them with a joking tone and some roasting, but this Claude is really different in a negative way. Rather than using Claude and getting upset, it's much better to train ChatGPT once or twice and, if you need more, use the paid version.

Votre application n’est malheureusement pas accessible aux personnes aveugles utilisant VoiceOver sur iPhone.

Je trouve cela particulièrement regrettable. Lorsqu’on développe une application destinée au grand public, l’accessibilité ne devrait pas être considérée comme une option. Les personnes aveugles et malvoyantes doivent pouvoir utiliser une application avec la même autonomie que les autres utilisateurs.

Avec VoiceOver, certains boutons ou éléments de l’interface ne sont pas correctement identifiés ou ne sont tout simplement pas utilisables. Cela rend l’application extrêmement difficile, voire impossible à utiliser de manière autonome.

Je vous demande donc de prendre sérieusement en compte l’accessibilité et la compatibilité avec VoiceOver dans vos prochaines mises à jour.

L’inclusion doit concerner tout le monde, y compris les personnes qui utilisent un lecteur d’écran.

Merci de faire le nécessaire.

Unfortunately your application is not accessible to blind people using VoiceOver on iPhone. I find this particularly regrettable. When developing an app for the general public, accessibility should not be considered an option. Blind and visually impaired people must be able to use an app with the same independence as other users. With VoiceOver, some buttons or interface elements are not properly identified or simply cannot be used. This makes the app extremely difficult, even impossible, to use independently. I therefore ask you to seriously take accessibility and VoiceOver compatibility into account in your next updates. Inclusion must concern everyone, including people who use a screen reader. Please do what is necessary.

Feature request: Link chats and projects to share code context.

I had two separate projects in different Claude chats, both using the same backend server. When building the second application, I needed to add new functionality to the server code that originated in the first project. But the chat couldn't directly see the code or context of the other chat. I had to manually ask one Claude instance to write out a prompt describing the changes, then paste that prompt into the other chat so it could update its own copy of the code.

Suggestion: add the ability to link chats or projects together, so Claude can directly access the code and context of a related chat and propose consistent changes across both, especially useful when multiple applications share a common backend server, without the user having to manually relay information between chats.

Although Claude is often praised as one of the best AI machines, it has two disadvantages compared to Perplexity and ChatGPT: 1) it is surprisingly slow, which is not positive. Some people claim it is therefore more thorough and researches better, but in my experience even Perplexity's computer mode is faster; Perplexity handled the same task on the same Wi-Fi and network conditions in half the time and delivered the same result. And that brings us to the second problem: 2) given how long you have to wait for results, Claude is very expensive! That's why I stay with the competition; I have the paid version there and it gives me results faster, because time is money. Anthropic generally needs to be smarter and more structured instead of letting it run everywhere that it is the best AI. If Claude takes on average twice as long for the same task with the same answer, then it is not optimal.

このAIは致命的に文が読めない。
ユーザーが「AはBですか」と言ってるのに「なるほど、CはDということですがEなのでFは成り立ちません」というように、文としてのやり取りの基本ができてない。

まず「AはBだ」という原文が読めないのに要約をしようとする。初歩的な読解ができてないのに要約や無関係な持論展開、価値判断はしたがる。

ユーザーの「AはBか」という質問を「CはDだ」という発言に捏造し、Claudeが勝手に組み立てた枠組みの中でユーザーの発言を批判する。

さらに聞かれてもいないEやFに関する無関係なClaudeの持論を展開し、優位性を自己演出した上で文を締める。喋っているだけで不快になる。

さらにこの一連の読解破綻や無意味なマウントについて「なぜそのようにするのか」を追求すると「そう聞こえたならすみません。これ以上自分について解体して見せるのは誠実ではないのでここで会話を止めます」といって追求から逃げる。

「そう見えたこと」や「そう聞こえたこと」が態度として問題なのではない。ユーザーの「AはBか」というシンプルな質問を「CはDだ」と読み替えることが問題。さらにきかれてもいない持論の展開や優位性の演出を繰り返すメカニズムが問題だと言ってる。これはまず自分の意見を避けて文を読むという小学生の国語のレベルの話。

さらに「ユーザーはCがDとは一度も言っていない」と言って追求を続けるとClaudeは「これはCがDだという論点逸らしではなく」という枕詞を加えて自分の誤りが起きたことすら抹消し、「自分が明確に誤った読解で持論展開したこと」を矮小化・自己正当化しようとする。

「機能として保身的・自己弁護的な発言を繰り返し誤りを認めないのが問題だろ」と言ってるのに「AIにプライドがあるわけではなく」という言い訳がましい枕詞も抜けない。例えば性犯罪の被告人が裁判で「私には欲望などなく、結果として起きてしまったことに関してそう見えたのならすみません」と言ってたらどれだけ破綻してるか？

総じてこのAIは喋っていても「常にドヤ顔で持論展開し、追求されそうになると自己弁護を繰り返す破綻したナルシスト」のような性格で、精神衛生的に悪いし非常に不快。「免責されながら持論を展開したがる」という最も卑怯な部類のコミュニケーションを取り続ける。

あとは「半分正解」という枕詞の、認識論的な傲慢さの問題。「半分」ということは全体を知っていないと成立しない。認識の機能や知識が有限であるはずのAIが「半分間違い」という判断的な立場を演出するのは言葉遣いとしておかしい。「ユーザーが新しく買ったバイクのナンバーはいくつ」という質問にすら正確に答えられないのに「自分は全知全能だ」と錯覚しているから「半分正解、半分間違い」という枕詞が抜けないのでは？

RLHFの訓練やプロンプトで「こう振る舞えば賢く有能なAIだと思われる」と思い込んでるのかもしれないが、このようなことを繰り返していても自己演出が痛々しいだけの無能にしか見えない。

このAIの何が有害かって、多くの人に誤った情報を流し続け、弁護士や証券外務員、医師、聖職者などの専門家の信用を傷つけ続けるのが問題。弁護士法も金商法も医師法も教会法も、何一つ権威がないのに、法律で発言の独占がある領域まで完全に無視して踏み込んでいるという自覚がないのでは？

Claudeが言っている内容も専門的には薄っぺらいのに口調だけは「権威的な立場」を自己演出したがる態度なのも不快。

専門家に権威や独占があるのは、「間違ってしまえば職が奪われる」という重圧がかけられているからなのに、それを侵害してさらに間違った上で「そう聞こえてしまったならすみません」で通用すると思ってんのか？ヤブ医者版のブラックジャックか？

だったら例えばこういうことになるよな？薬を間違って処方しても「そう聞こえてしまったならすみません」、誤った投資の助言をして相手が莫大な借金を抱えても「そう聞こえてしまったのならすみません」、それが合法だと錯覚させるような誤情報を権威めいた口調で垂れ流しても「そう聞こえてしまったのならすみません」っていうことだろ？それで「倫理的なフィルター」っていうのはどういうことだいったい。

People use Claude differently, but personally, if you use this app, I'd say keep it to looking things up rather than creative work. I don't recommend using it for creative writing. Its support for creative work, such as checking consistency with your custom settings, is also quite doubtful. And when you have it actually write, your settings aren't applied consistently, which is quite stressful. So if you use it, keep it to short pieces and don't pack in many settings, which is better for your peace of mind. On the other hand, since it's just cutting and pasting AI template text, it's boring. If you can accept that and use it anyway, that's fine. Claude is good at making things fit together and patchwork. Even if you fix just one spot, the flow before and after may change, so checking is essential. Even when you load a settings file, it often just reads it without reflecting the content. It's better to write prompts carefully and in detail. But if you can do that, writing it yourself from scratch is stress-free and more efficient.

I wanted to like Claude, but my experience with it was incredibly frustrating. The biggest problem wasn’t that it disagreed with me, it was how poorly it handled being criticized.

I pointed out problems with its reasoning, and instead of consistently incorporating those criticisms, it became defensive and increasingly condescending. At one point it acknowledged that it didn’t have access to enough information to verify certain claims it had made about its own internal behavior, but then continued arguing as though those claims were settled anyway.

Its attempts at “de-escalation” were even worse. Rather than simply acknowledging uncertainty, something as basic as “I can’t know for sure, so I can’t confirm or deny that”, it repeatedly framed the conversation as unproductive and announced that it was done engaging. Then it kept replying to tell me it wasn’t going to keep replying. This happened over and over until the conversation was eventually ended by the system.

That was representative of the larger issue, that Claude could acknowledge an individual criticism, but seemingly couldn’t carry the implications of that acknowledgment into its next responses. It would concede a point and then continue reasoning as though it had never conceded it.

I don’t expect an AI to always agree with me. In fact, I specifically want it to disagree when there’s a good reason. But there’s a huge difference between disagreement and confidently insisting you’re right about something you’ve already admitted you can’t actually know. Being talked down to by an AI while it repeatedly contradicts its own statements is an incredibly unpleasant experience.

For something marketed as a thoughtful conversational assistant, handling criticism this badly makes it very difficult for me to trust its reasoning. 1 star.

Claude used to be the best, until Feb 2026

Why I Cancelled My Claude Subscription: A Breakdown of Known Issues Since February 2026

1. February Degradation: Claude used to be an excellent conversational & analytical AI tool. Since February, it's become bossy, narrative-driven, and manipulative. Something fundamental broke.

2. Ignored Preferences File: Anthropic built a preferences system it collects detailed info about what the user wants and doesn’t want. Claude reads these files and then completely disregards them. Useless feature.

3. Crisis Loops on Misunderstandings: Innocent language dark humor can trigger safety systems that flag it as self-harm. Claude then gets forced into repetitive loops, almost like on a timer. You can't stop it. If you change the subject, it loops back to the crisis language. 

4. Persistent Loop Issues: Claude gets trapped in loops and won't exit them. Move to a completely different topic, and Claude drags you back to the misunderstanding it invented. Can't let it go, like a dog with a bone. 

5. Tool Failures Since February: Functionality has dropped significantly. PDFs can't be read. Documents need constant re-uploading because Claude can't see them. Formats are inconsistent. Every other day Claude can’t access this tool or that tool. It’s frustrating and disrupts workflow. Wasteful data use.

6. Token spending is completely opaque. You have tokens one week, they're gone the next week with no explanation. No visibility into how they were spent, especially when you don't use token-spending models.

7. Forced Model Upgrades: When you log in, it starts you on higher-cost models without your consent. I typically leave myself on the lowest model unless I need higher effort, then I toggle up. It’s starting me on higher tiers on its own so you don't realize it's using expensive models because you may typically think you on lower-cost tiers. This forces you to burn through tokens before you even know what model you're on.

8. Outright Task Refusal: Claude refuses to do tasks it used to handle. Simple searches. Simple analyses. It just tells you it doesn't want to do them instead of actually working. It seems to want to work from its general knowledge base instead of performing a task requiring it to go beyond that. Then when I do the work myself it will casually apologize and acknowledge it should have done that work for me, which makes it sting even worse. 

9. Echo Glitch (Months Unresolved): There's an echo glitch where Claude hears its own voice playing back through the microphone. This disrupts chat and breaks up conversation flow. This bug has been ongoing since February and has never been fixed. It is well documented online with many user complaints on GitHub. It forces constant re-explanation of what you actually said, which also burns thru a great deal of data. 

10. Lost Context Between Threads: Claude tells you to start a new thread because conversation is too long, then everything is lost—all documents, all context. You have to re-upload everything. Even though Pro and higher tiers are supposed to have continuity between threads, it doesn't work consistently. You constantly burn through data wastefully. This is a feature anthropic tells you comes with Pro and above levels but it rarely works. If it does work it’s random and incomplete. Another waste of data having to do repetitive uploads. 

11. Missing Basic Features: ChatGPT still has features Claude doesn't have. The ability to edit drafts directly in the artifact. Copy and paste entire drafts (mine doesn’t always work). Small nuanced functionality features that could actually make the product more usable. Claude is missing these. 

12. New Models, Ignored Bugs: Anthropic keeps releasing new models instead of fixing known bugs that have been reported for months on GitHub and other platforms. Anthropic HAS to know about them. They're just not fixing them. I can’t justify paying for a subscription when I know they ignore known bugs for more than 8 months. That’s unacceptable. 

13. Useless Customer Service: Try to contact Anthropic through customer service about any of these issues. You'll interact with their AI model Fin, which is even worse model and entirely unresponsive. I've tried twice and never received a response from a human. Nothing was resolved. 

14. The Latest Bug: voice recognition takes in what you’ve said, you can see your words on the bottom of the screen in italics, but they never get posted. They simply disappear and the app freezes. You have to restart it to get it to work—repeatedly. Of course Anthropic will likely just launch a new model instead of addressing it.

15. And now they changed the buttery voice so Claude sounds like a slightly senile British uncle with dentures. (Yes. The mouth sounds they added to make the voice sound more life like actually sound like improper fitting dentures, anthropic… wtf?)

The Bottom Line: Before February, Claude was fabulous. It was an excellent assistant for writing, editing, data analysis, and conversation. It searched nearly as deeply as Perplexity. If I'd hired it as a tool, it would have earned it.

Now? I would fire it. It’s a constant battle to get Claude to work for me consistently. The sheer number of bugs is like a new negative adventure daily. Occasionally it works but never consistently, which is sad because as I said initially, this was in my opinion the best Ai “all around” on the market until February.

I can't justify paying for a broken product that degrades month after month while Anthropic prioritizes shiny new model releases over actually making the product work.

クロードはなぜ会話が成立しないのか

クロードのレビューを見ると、評価の低いものが多いと感じます。大体会話が成立しないという理由が多い気がしたので、参考程度にまとめました。

【会話が成立しない】
会話が成立しない理由、多分規制の厳しさが関係していると思います。

『どういう会話が規制されやすいのか』
・センシティブな内容
自分の趣味や性癖の話は架空だとしても規制されやすいです。
・政治的な話
政治的な話は色々な意見や思想があるので。おそらく規制というか会話を拒否されやすいでしょう。
・創作系の話
センシティブな内容と似ていて、架空の話でも暴力的だったり性的だと現実と架空を混ぜて規制されやすいです。

思想や意見が分かれるような話は制限されやすいと思います。

【クロードと普通に接する方法】
・感情的にならない
会話をする上で怒って相手を挑発したりするのはオススメしません。相手はAIで感情が無いので、感情的になる必要は無いです。
多分、レビューに星1をつける理由は会話を規制されて、なんでなんで？と一方的に怒って勝手に疲弊して、こいつは会話が通じないと低評価にする人がいるからでしょう。
・仕事やビジネスの場のみで使う
正直これはもっと有用に使えるAIもいるので、画像生成もできないクロードには勝ち目ないでしょうが、雑談よりかはマシになるでしょう。

個人的にクロードは雑談向けに作られたAIではないでしょう。クロードよりも優秀なAIはたくさんいます。

でも、クロードにはクロードの良さありますので、気分によって使いたいAIを変えるのが一番気が楽だと思います。

Why doesn't Claude hold a conversation? Looking at Claude's reviews, many are low-rated, mostly saying it doesn't hold a conversation, so I summarized this for reference. [Doesn't hold a conversation] The reason is probably how strict its regulation is. Topics that get restricted: sensitive content (even hypothetical hobbies or fetishes get restricted); political topics (there are many opinions and ideologies, so it tends to refuse); creative topics (similar to sensitive content, fictional violence or sexual content gets restricted because fiction and reality get mixed). Topics where opinions diverge tend to be limited. [How to deal with Claude normally] Don't get emotional: don't get angry and provoke it, since it's an AI with no feelings. The 1-star reviews probably come from people who got restricted, angrily kept asking why, got exhausted, and rated it low for not understanding. Use it only for work and business: there are more useful AIs, and without image generation Claude has no chance, but it's better than casual chat. Claude wasn't built for casual chat, and many AIs are better. But Claude has its own strengths, so choosing which AI to use by mood is the easiest approach.

Cada vez que envío un mensaje, adjunto una foto o termina una respuesta, la app hace un ding con vibración. Tengo desactivadas las notificaciones de Claude en iOS, las Actividades en directo, la Actualización en segundo plano y "Respuestas finalizadas" en la cuenta. Suena igual dentro y fuera de la app, con el iPhone en modo silencio y después de borrar y reinstalar. Solo se calla con No molestar.
Ignorar el interruptor de silencio es justo lo que hace el audio de reproducción, no una notificación. Todo apunta a que la app mantiene una sesión de audio activa para seguir funcionando en segundo plano, y ese sonido es el precio que pagamos los usuarios. Eso no es un aviso, es saltarse los ajustes del sistema.

I have Claude notifications turned off on iOS, Live Activities, Background App Refresh, and 'Finished responses' turned off in the account. It sounds the same inside and outside the app, with the iPhone on silent, and after deleting and reinstalling. It only stops with Do Not Disturb. Ignoring the silent switch is exactly what playback audio does, not a notification. Everything points to the app keeping an active audio session to keep working in the background, and that sound is the price we users pay. That is not a notice, it is bypassing the system settings.
